source_title: Reducing Emergency Department (ED) Boarding Time Through Lean Redesign of the ED-to-Inpatient Admission Pathway: A Single-Center Quality-Improvement Study
locator: Methods (study period and cohort flow); Results, Cohort flow and admission cycle time; Table 2 and Table 3. Endpoint: admission order to arrival in inpatient bed.
source_setting: Adult ED-to-inpatient admissions at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre, a tertiary hospital; single-center pre/post quality-improvement project.
source_n: 435 analyzed encounters (217 baseline, 218 post-intervention) from 500 identified; 65 excluded.
quantity: Median admission-order-to-inpatient-bed-arrival cycle time, baseline vs post-intervention
source_evidence_basis: EHR-derived patient-level admission cycle time fell from 390 to 175 minutes after a bundled redesign; the paper reports this as a 215-minute (55.1%) decrease. The reported intervention included earlier bed coordination, streamlined testing, and transfer checklist changes.
limitations: Single-center pre/post QI association; no causal inference, and the bundled intervention prevents component attribution. COVID testing gate was specific to the study context. These observed medians are not a probability distribution and are not RWJ data.
inferred_scenario_use: External reference for admission-to-bed cycle-time scenarios; retain baseline/post as separate contextual benchmarks, and decompose locally into bed request, assignment, EVS, ready signal, handoff, and transport only when local timestamps exist.

source_title: Reducing Emergency Department (ED) Boarding Time Through Lean Redesign of the ED-to-Inpatient Admission Pathway: A Single-Center Quality-Improvement Study
locator: Results, Monthly Pareto charts; Figures 3A-3C (January-March 2023 delay events).
source_setting: Same single-center adult ED admission pathway; monthly operational delay-event tallies.
source_n: 86 categorized inefficiency events: January 31, February 31, March 24; event counts, not patient-level cohort denominators.
quantity: Share of monthly delay events attributed to bed/receiving-unit readiness categories
unit: percent of categorized monthly delay events
source_evidence_basis: The paper's operational Pareto tallies identify receiving-unit delay, bed not ready, and last-minute orders as the leading recorded categories in the baseline months.
limitations: These are categorized delay events, not unique patients or duration shares; local coding definitions and this hospital's workflows may differ. Monthly denominator is small. Not an RWJ observation.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent admission delays as competing transition blockers (receiving-unit acceptance, bed readiness, late orders); use the reported proportions only as qualitative external prioritization, not local probabilities or time distributions.

source_title: Reduced isolation room turnover time using Lean methodology
locator: Abstract, Design/Setting/Results; room turnover endpoint defined from discharged patient exit to UV disinfection completion.
source_setting: Quaternary academic pediatric referral facility, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; transmission-based precaution isolation rooms.
source_period: 60-day quality-improvement before/after project; published 2019. Exact calendar dates and observation counts are not stated in the accessible abstract.
source_n: Manual time-study sample size not stated in the accessible abstract; before/after observations were performed.
quantity: Median isolation-room turnover to UV disinfection completion, before vs after
source_evidence_basis: The original study reports measured manual time-study medians and ranges. Turnover includes breakdown, cleaning, and waiting through completion of UV disinfection, not just surface-cleaning labor.
limitations: Pediatric isolation-room workflow with UV disinfection; before/after improvement project, sample counts unavailable in abstract, and the median/range are not a fitted distribution. Not a generic adult bed-cleaning time or RWJ fact.
inferred_scenario_use: Model cleaning/turnaround as a gated room-readiness transition with separate cleaning and post-clean disinfection steps where locally applicable. Use the observed result only as an external isolation-room benchmark, not a standard bed-turnaround parameter.

source_title: Reduced isolation room turnover time using Lean methodology
locator: Abstract, Results; duration of room cleaning and curtain changing.
source_setting: Quaternary academic pediatric referral facility; isolation-room cleaning and curtain changing.
source_period: 60-day quality-improvement before/after project; exact dates not stated in accessible abstract.
source_n: Manual time-study sample size not stated in accessible abstract.
quantity: Median active room-cleaning and curtain-changing duration, before vs after
source_evidence_basis: The study reports measured median duration for the room-cleaning and curtain-changing task, separate from total room turnover. It also reports median wait from cleaning complete to UV start of 36 minutes before and 8 minutes after (Abstract, Results).
limitations: Isolation-room pediatric task with curtain replacement; intervention-specific and not an adult routine clean. Accessible abstract gives no sample count or distribution; no inference to other facilities.
inferred_scenario_use: Keep active EVS task duration separate from queue/wait for cleaning start and any required post-clean disinfection. Treat observed medians as scenario references only; do not sum medians as a patient-level total or assign a distribution.

source_title: An Observational Study of the Factors Affecting Staffing Demands During Intrahospital Transfers
locator: Methods (observed transfer definition); Results and Table 3. Observation ended when origin nurse returned to origin unit.
source_setting: 718-bed Level I trauma hospital; 39 between-unit and 11 within-unit transfers observed, including ICU/PCU transfers.
source_period: Publication 2025; observation dates/collection window not specified in the accessible full text.
source_n: 50 complete observed transfers; 5 additional observations excluded for discontinuity or destination change; 7 pilot observations not included.
quantity: Mean total transfer-related staff time and RN time per observed transfer
unit: minutes of staff labor per transfer (means)
source_evidence_basis: Direct structured observation summed staff time spent on transfer-related tasks. The study notes that total staff labor can exceed elapsed transfer time because multiple people work simultaneously.
limitations: Small convenience observation sample at a trauma hospital, principally daytime; staff labor minutes are not elapsed patient journey duration. The value is a mean, not a distribution or universal transfer-time estimate.
inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external labor-demand anchor for transfer episodes, keeping staff-minutes distinct from patient elapsed time. Represent acuity changes, equipment/belongings setup, handoff, destination readiness, and elevator use as transition/resource factors.

source_title: An Observational Study of the Factors Affecting Staffing Demands During Intrahospital Transfers
locator: Table 3 (activity time means and SDs); Results (elevator-use stratification).
source_setting: Same 718-bed Level I trauma hospital observed intrahospital transfers.
source_period: Observation dates/collection window not specified in accessible full text; article published 2025.
source_n: Activity denominators vary: patient transport n=50; elevator/no-elevator regression subgroup counts not stated in Results passage.
quantity: Observed transport-with-patient task and total staff-time by elevator use
unit: minutes; task mean (SD) and total staff-time means stratified by elevator use
source_evidence_basis: Table 3 reports mean staff time to move the patient from room to destination room. A regression analysis in Results reports higher mean total staff and nurse labor when an elevator was used.
limitations: Transport task time is one subtask and is not the full transfer. Elevator figures are staff labor means, not elapsed trip time; subgroup denominators are not reported in the cited Results passage. Small single-hospital sample; no distribution inference.
inferred_scenario_use: Separate moving time from room preparation, handoff, setup, return tasks, and staff labor. Use elevator as a context-sensitive factor to test, not a universal fixed multiplier or RWJ-specific estimate.

source_title: The effect of discharge destination and primary insurance provider on hospital discharge delays among patients with traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study of 1,543 patients
locator: Abstract, Methods/Results; Results, Discharge delays; Table 1. Delay defined as discharge at least 24h after case-management documentation of readiness.
source_setting: Four Level I trauma centers across three US states; adults with TBI and ISS >=9.
quantity: Median post-readiness discharge delay among delayed TBI patients
source_evidence_basis: Retrospective cohort measured discharge delay from case-management documentation that the patient was ready to actual discharge; median time from admission to delay start was 6 days, and median delay duration was 3 days.
limitations: Restricted to adult TBI patients at trauma centers and delay threshold >=24 h. Destination availability, insurance, and regional practices vary. The result is a conditional median among delayed cases, not a general all-patient distribution or RWJ measurement.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent clinical readiness and physical discharge as distinct states; allow downstream authorization, accepting-facility bed availability, and family coordination blockers. Use the median only as a conditional external stress-case benchmark.

source_title: The effect of discharge destination and primary insurance provider on hospital discharge delays among patients with traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study of 1,543 patients
locator: Abstract, Results; Results, Discharge delays and Table 1.
source_setting: Same four Level I trauma centers; delayed adults with TBI.
source_n: 210 delayed patients; reasons could overlap (percentages are not mutually exclusive).
source_evidence_basis: Medical-record review identified insurance processing/authorization, no accepting facility bed, and patient-related barriers such as language or family coordination as commonly reported delay reasons.
limitations: Reasons may co-occur; denominator is delayed TBI patients, not all admissions. Percentages should not be normalized to sum to 100 or treated as local rates. Not RWJ data.
inferred_scenario_use: Use as evidence that discharge planning needs parallel social-work/family, payer authorization, and post-acute placement transitions. Preserve overlapping blockers and external population scope; calibrate from local workflow data.

source_title: Hospital discharge and community support guidance
locator: Sections 5-6 (structure, roles, best practice); Annex A (operational discharge-to-assess process); Annex B (pathways 0-3); Annex C (discharge-process responsibilities).
source_setting: Official England NHS/local-authority hospital discharge guidance; describes acute/community hospitals and integrated care pathways.
source_period: Official guidance, accessed 2026-10-10; guidance applies in England.
source_n: Not applicable; official operating guidance, not an outcome study.
quantity: Documented discharge-planning and placement transition stages
value: start discharge planning at or before admission
identify current support and post-discharge needs with patient/family
coordinate health and social care through a multidisciplinary team/care transfer hub
select pathway: usual home, home with support, bed-based intermediate rehabilitation, or new residential/nursing placement
check service/bed availability and coordinate transfer
include social-work, safeguarding, advocacy, and carer needs where relevant
source_evidence_basis: The official guidance specifies four discharge-to-assess pathways and assigns coordination roles across hospital, health, social care, community providers, and care-transfer hubs; it directs early planning, needs assessment, and vacancy checks.
limitations: Policy guidance for England, not an observed hospital execution-time study and not US/RWJ policy. Local law, terminology, pathway design, staffing, eligibility and service capacity differ.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent discharge readiness, destination selection, referral, acceptance/authorization, transport, and post-discharge support as explicit linked states. Treat pathway choices and roles as candidate process structure requiring local workflow confirmation.
